spec_interactions.spec_clause: EDIT SESSIONS 1-3 / REVIEW STAGE 6 (session = stages; submit review; exit)
spec_interactions.current_behaviour: A 'run' (RunView) is the session. Each round's proposal in run.state 'review' is the review stage. The end-of-stage actions are Feedback (free text, new round), Accept (all-or-nothing write; ends the run) and Discard (ends the run; no write). Cancel stops a working run. Every run needs a target and premises: it starts from 'These suffice ▶' or 'Self-evident?'.
spec_interactions.conflict_or_gap: There is no 'submit review' with per-item results, and no session without a target (a TRANSFORM-initiated session has no counterpart). Mapping: review stage ~ round; exit ~ Discard; successful end ~ Accept of a fully accepted state.
spec_interactions.safety_relevance: The final write must still be one complete state that passed the gate. Today's Accept writes exactly the checked files and re-gates on drift.

spec_interactions.spec_clause: REVIEW STAGE 1 (Claude proposes changes, new cards, deletions)
spec_interactions.current_behaviour: G5 forbids Claude adding or removing @@ telelean blocks and changing any markup field (natural_name and rationale are byte-identical). G3 'existing-changed' forbids changing or removing any declaration that existed at run start (B) other than T.holds. So a proposal can contain only: new statements for code-less cards ('Formalize'), new vocabulary, definitions, presuppositions and lemmas, proofs, telelean-written adopted ghosts, and the telelean lifecycle kind change.
spec_interactions.conflict_or_gap: 'Change <card>' beyond formalising, 'Delete <card>' and Claude-created 'Add <card>' are impossible today; they need a redesign of G3/G5. The '− removed' diff marks can currently arise only from cards the user added to the real board during the run, which looks like a spurious mark.
spec_interactions.safety_relevance: High. Today's soundness rests on 'Claude never changes the user's words or existing declarations; new beliefs only through user adoption'. A replacement invariant is needed: every difference from B is covered by an item the user explicitly accepted, checked mechanically by the gate.

spec_interactions.spec_clause: REVIEW STAGE 2 (scrollable list labelled Add/Change/Delete/Formalize <card>; status table)
spec_interactions.current_behaviour: A wrapping row of pills, one step body at a time, and Back/Next. The labels are 'Statement N' (or 'Statement'), 'New vocabulary', 'Definitions (N)', 'Result', 'Card changes'. Progress reads 'Step i of n: label'. There is no per-step status.
spec_interactions.conflict_or_gap: Mapping: Formalize ~ StatementReview.change 'new' on an existing card; an adopted ghost is also 'new' today but would be 'Add'; 'changed' ~ Change (effectively unreachable today); lifecycle 'Make … a Derivation' ~ Change (kind). The 'Result' step (report card: verdict, footprint, unused premises, assumed without asking with 'Ask me instead', gate attempts, files) has no place in the spec, and neither do proofs (they are not review items).
spec_interactions.safety_relevance: D-19 'meaning before proof status' hides proof results until the statements are reviewed. The spec does not say whether the list or status table may show proof status beside the statements (automation bias).

spec_interactions.spec_clause: REVIEW STAGE 2 ('one item for all the vocabulary')
spec_interactions.current_behaviour: VocabularyReview is already a single item, but it covers only pure-signature items (sort/predicate/function/constant). These are auto-approved, and revocable only by a prefilled Feedback. Definitions on a statement path and new presupposition axioms are separate DefinitionQuestions, each needing 'Yes, I endorse it'; Accept is blocked until all are yes. Off-path definitions and lemmas get no review item, only '+ new' in the Proposed view's Vocabulary group.
spec_interactions.conflict_or_gap: The spec does not say whether definitions and existence assumptions go into the single vocabulary item or get items of their own.
spec_interactions.safety_relevance: High. The UI's own rule is 'A definition can quietly carry a belief, so Accept needs your yes for each'. A presupposition (e.g. T.exists) is an axiom, that is, a belief. Bundling them into one vocabulary accept (or a group accept) would weaken the per-item endorsement. Recommend keeping each definition and presupposition as its own item.

spec_interactions.spec_clause: REVIEW STAGE 2 ('Claude suggests' treated as regular new cards with their own entries)
spec_interactions.current_behaviour: A ghost is not a card and not in the proposal's files. It is checked in a scratch file (selected premises + ghost ⊢ target). It is shown translucent at the top of the Assumptions column (Proposed view only; no data-node-id; not selectable) and in the report card after the reveal. 'I hold this' makes telelean write the card (worded_by agent) and the target's premises:, re-freeze with the ghost selected, and start a new round. 'No' marks it rejected; Claude is not told.
spec_interactions.conflict_or_gap: If suggestions become 'Add <card>' items inside the proposal files, the round's proof could rest on an assumption nobody has accepted yet. Ghosts cannot be selected or TRANSFORMed today. A suggested ghost is not invalidated when a later round changes the statements: its 'closes the gap (checked)' chip can be stale.
spec_interactions.safety_relevance: High. A Claude-created ASSUMPTION's .holds must stay out of the permitted set until it is explicitly accepted. A verdict that rests on a pending Add must be shown as conditional and recomputed if the Add is declined. Today: G3 new-axiom, plus adoption followed by a re-freeze.

spec_interactions.spec_clause: REVIEW STAGE 3 (per-item accept/decline; accepted ⇒ FROZEN; cannot end while any item is 'in review')
spec_interactions.current_behaviour: No per-item accept, except definitions (yes/no, all must be yes), lifecycle ticks and ghost adopt/reject. Accept is all-or-nothing (D-21; 'node-level partial accept comes later'). The review state (ReviewUi) is webview memory only, lost on reload, and the host records no endorsements.
spec_interactions.conflict_or_gap: Item statuses must live and be enforced on the host side, in run.json and in a gate rule (like existing-changed/G5) that compares against an 'accepted snapshot'. They must also be bound to exact content (a hash), so that 'accepted' never carries over to changed text in the next stage.
spec_interactions.safety_relevance: The webview is untrusted (protocol.ts header). A status that exists only in the UI cannot guarantee 'Claude can never edit a frozen card'.

spec_interactions.spec_clause: REVIEW STAGE 4 (multi-select; group accept/decline; multi-card TRANSFORM)
spec_interactions.current_behaviour: The Proposed view is read-only: a click does not select (NodeCard.tsx:139-141); there is no drag or edit. Ghost cards and vocabulary items are not selectable. Review steps are not selectable. Selection is a list of card ids on the Current graph only.
spec_interactions.conflict_or_gap: Selecting, and group actions, inside the review view or Proposed view need new UI and state.
spec_interactions.safety_relevance: A group accept could sweep in belief-carrying items (definitions, presuppositions, new assumptions). Consider excluding them from group accept or requiring per-item confirmation.

spec_interactions.spec_clause: REVIEW STAGE 5 ('These suffice' during a review stage)
spec_interactions.current_behaviour: The tray's run buttons are disabled for any active run, review included: "Claude's proposal… is waiting for your review: accept, give feedback or discard it first." There is at most one run per model root, and the tray works on the Current graph.
spec_interactions.conflict_or_gap: No in-session 'These suffice' exists. It would need a new round that still goes through formalise, freeze_statements, prove and the gate.
spec_interactions.safety_relevance: The statement freeze before proving (D-19, checked by the G4 comparator) must still apply to a mid-session inference.

spec_interactions.spec_clause: REVIEW STAGE 6 (Claude acts on non-accepted items, then the next stage)
spec_interactions.current_behaviour: Feedback is free text. The next round restarts in the 'formalise' stage with the statement freeze cleared, so Claude may revise any statement, including ones the user was happy with. Feedback is the only channel for a definition 'No…', vocabulary 'Revoke…' and 'Ask me instead'; each only prefills the draft.
spec_interactions.conflict_or_gap: Nothing structured tells Claude which items were accepted or declined, or why. The prefilled sentences are the only per-item signal.
spec_interactions.safety_relevance: Without mechanical freezing, Claude can silently change already-approved statements in the next round. Today a new review of every new statement covers this.

spec_interactions.spec_clause: REVIEW STAGE 7-8 (restore frozen state at session end; confirmation popup listing auto freeze/unfreeze)
spec_interactions.current_behaviour: There is no user-level freeze. The run's statement freeze never touches the user's files. Accept, Discard, Cancel and Stop have no confirmation dialog, only tooltips (acceptTitle) and afterwards the outcome line or toast. The DialogState kinds are dependents, rationale, delete and revert.
spec_interactions.conflict_or_gap: A new confirmation dialog is needed, plus durable storage of the pre-session frozen map.
spec_interactions.safety_relevance: Low directly. Restoring state after a crash must be durable on the host side.

spec_interactions.spec_clause: DECLINE OPTIONS 1 (don't create this card for the rest of the session: blacklist)
spec_interactions.current_behaviour: Ghost 'No' sets the state to 'rejected'; it disappears from the board and report card and the proposal stays open. Claude is not told, and propose_assumption does not refuse a previously rejected statement (only Lean-name uniqueness is checked). Nothing else can be blacklisted.
spec_interactions.conflict_or_gap: A blacklist has to be enforced on the host side, for example by refusing a matching Add or propose_assumption. Today nothing enforces one.
spec_interactions.safety_relevance: Medium: it stops beliefs the user declined from being re-proposed.

spec_interactions.current_behaviour: Only free-text Feedback, prefilled per item: ``I don't endorse the definition `X` (“…”): `` / ``Please don't add the vocabulary item `X` (“…”): `` / 'You assumed this without asking: “…”. Please ask me about it instead of assuming it.'
spec_interactions.conflict_or_gap: There is no structured edit of a proposed item. The Proposed view and review are read-only.
spec_interactions.safety_relevance: Fields the user fills in must be recorded as the user's words (provenance), and fuzzy fields that Claude fills in as Claude's (worded_by agent).

spec_interactions.current_behaviour: Nothing like it. Feedback rounds let Claude reproduce anything.
spec_interactions.conflict_or_gap: Needs a mechanical comparison on the host side between the previous shaky configuration and the new one.
spec_interactions.safety_relevance: Low (a usability constraint), but it should be enforced by the host, not by the prompt.

spec_interactions.spec_clause: TRANSFORM 9-10 (any card including 'Claude suggests' and Vocabulary; no edits to Depends on / Used by)
spec_interactions.current_behaviour: Ghosts are not cards (no data-node-id; stopPropagation). Vocabulary items are boxes in the Vocabulary group with code, Used by and Open in editor, and are not editable. 'Depends on' and 'Used by' are computed (CardDetails Relations).
spec_interactions.conflict_or_gap: Ghosts and vocabulary need to become selectable and transformable entities.
spec_interactions.safety_relevance: Editing vocabulary changes the meaning of every statement that uses it. Dependents' items should go back to 'in review'.

spec_interactions.spec_clause: FROZEN 1 (aura must not clash with the Lean-formalisation aura) and the name 'FROZEN'
spec_interactions.current_behaviour: Existing visuals: the blue formalised aura (--tl-aura, charts-blue); git green, amber and red diff halos in the Proposed view; the selection outline (focusBorder); the orange flash highlight; kind colours A purple, D green, G orange; translucent ghost cards with a purple bar. 'Freeze' already names the per-round statement freeze: freeze_statements, RunView.frozen, G4 'frozen before the proof', the commit 'Statements frozen (round N)', the activity kind 'freeze' (lock icon).
spec_interactions.conflict_or_gap: The spec's FROZEN collides in name with the existing freeze_statements concept, and its aura must avoid every colour above.
spec_interactions.safety_relevance: Confusing the user-level lock with the proof-time statement freeze could mislead the user about what is guaranteed. Recommend a distinct term (e.g. 'Locked').

spec_interactions.spec_clause: FROZEN 2-3 (Claude never edits a frozen card, enforced mechanically; unfreeze only by the user)
spec_interactions.current_behaviour: The existing mechanical analogues are G5 (user's words and markup untouched), G3 existing-changed (B's declarations untouched) and G4 (lake comparator against the round's freeze). None of them is driven by user-chosen per-card or per-field locks.
spec_interactions.conflict_or_gap: Needs a new gate rule against a user-lock snapshot, and a channel for Claude to request an unfreeze (ask_user or a new tool).
spec_interactions.safety_relevance: High. It must be a rule in the gate, never a prompt instruction. It also interacts with proofs: a frozen target proof can break when a premise is unfrozen and changed, so the final Accept must re-gate everything.

spec_interactions.spec_clause: FROZEN 4-5 (select cards or fields and freeze/unfreeze at ALL times in ALL interfaces)
spec_interactions.current_behaviour: Selection is card ids only, on the Current view only. The Proposed view, review steps, ghost cards and vocabulary items cannot be selected. Fields cannot be selected at all.
spec_interactions.conflict_or_gap: Needs field-level selection and selection inside the review panel and Proposed view.

spec_interactions.spec_clause: INITIATING EDIT SESSIONS 3 (no direct field edits on the 'Current' tab)
spec_interactions.current_behaviour: Current is fully editable at all times, including during a run and during review (D-16: the A|D|G box works during a run; D-21 'Hand edits are authoritative'). Edits during a run count as drift: Accept rebases (3-way, no fuzz) and re-freezes and re-gates. Proposed is read-only.
spec_interactions.conflict_or_gap: This contradicts D-16 and D-21 and the current UX (F2/Edit, Add why, stance/source chips, Make <kind>, Delete, drag, the A|D|G box). VS Code's text editor can still change the files, so drift handling must remain.
spec_interactions.safety_relevance: Keep the drift re-gate at Accept whatever the UI allows.

spec_interactions.current_behaviour: The Feedback composer is a plain textarea (maximum 4000). Prefills name items with backtick Lean names. No mention or reference picker exists anywhere in the run UI.
spec_interactions.conflict_or_gap: New feature. The Feedback composer and the TRANSFORM prose box are the natural hosts.
spec_interactions.safety_relevance: None directly. References inside the prompt text must be resolved by the host into exact ids or names.

safety_invariants.enforced_where: UI: packages/webview/src/model/run.ts:500-502 (definitionsApproved), Review.tsx:267-298, ProposalBanner.tsx:24,59, store.ts:1529. Host: packages/runner/src/run/manager.ts:1651-1652. Producer: packages/core/src/gate/rules.ts:808-834.

safety_invariants.invariant: Accept writes exactly a state that passed the gate (the checked files plus ticked lifecycle items), never part of a proposal. If the user's files drifted, Claude's changes are rebased and re-frozen and re-gated first.
safety_invariants.how_new_spec_could_break_it: Per-item accept or decline tempts splicing accepted pieces into the real files. The final write must instead be a whole state that the gate re-checked after Claude removed the declined items.

safety_invariants.invariant: A new belief (an ASSUMPTION or its .holds axiom) enters only by explicit user adoption. Claude cannot add blocks or .holds axioms for cards that are not selected. A suggestion is checked only in a scratch file and joins the permitted set only after adoption and a re-freeze.
safety_invariants.enforced_where: packages/core/src/gate/rules.ts:836-945 (G5, no new blocks except teleleanBlocks) and G3 new-axiom; packages/runner/src/gate/scratch.ts:49-67; packages/runner/src/run/manager.ts:1530-1613.

safety_invariants.invariant: Claude never changes the user's words or markup (natural_name, rationale, fields, ids, lean lines, notes) and never changes or removes any declaration that existed at run start (other than T.holds).
safety_invariants.how_new_spec_could_break_it: 'Change <card>' and 'Delete <card>' items and TRANSFORM need these rules relaxed. Without a replacement 'every difference is covered by an accepted item' check, unreviewed edits could slip through.

safety_invariants.enforced_where: packages/runner/src/gate/engine.ts (freeze, gate G4); packages/runner/src/run/manager.ts:1509-1522 (startNewRound clears the freeze); packages/core/src/run.ts:132,301-302.

(Small leak: ghost cards on the board ignore the reveal.)

answers:
Q1. What does the "Fully explicit" checkbox do?
It appears in each "Statement N" step of the review, under the box labelled "Lean statement <name>". Its tooltip reads "No notation, every argument and universe shown, no coercion arrows". It switches that box between two printouts of the same Lean statement. Both are produced by Lean itself from Claude's working copy after the round, not written by Claude:
- Normal: Lean's default printing, `#print <statement>`.
- Fully explicit: the same `#print` with these options set: `pp.explicit true` (hidden arguments shown with @), `pp.notation false` (symbols written as the functions they stand for), `pp.universes true` (universe levels shown) and `pp.coercions false` (type conversions shown as explicit functions instead of ↑). The options are fixed in `packages/runner/src/gate/scratch.ts:112`; the forms are built in `proposal/service.ts:224-233`.

The visible effect: `¬P` becomes `Not (P)`, `∧/∨/↔` become `And/Or/Iff`, `∃ x, …` becomes `Exists fun x => …`, and `a = b` becomes `@Eq T a b`, which shows the type T. A real example from the tests: `… → ¬Spyro.InGame c g` versus `… → Not (Spyro.InGame c g)`. Names are fully qualified in both forms. The user guide's "every name in full" is not actually a difference.

When it helps: when notation could hide what the Lean says. Examples are what a `¬` covers, how ∧, ∨ and → group, the order of quantifiers, the type an equality or numeral is taken at, and hidden conversions or instance choices. With telelean's simple vocabulary rule, hidden arguments, universes and conversions rarely occur, so in practice it mostly spells out the logical symbols.

What it does not do:
- It changes only the display, one statement at a time. It is off by default, resets for every new proposal (and on a webview reload), sends nothing and does not affect Accept.
- It exists only on Statement steps. Definitions, vocabulary and suggestions show their raw source.
- If Lean could not print a statement, both forms fall back to the source text, and the toggle shows no change.

Its purpose (design decision D-19) is the faithfulness check the step asks: "Does the Lean say what the sentence says?".

Q2. "Claude suggests" cards versus "Statement 1", "Statement 2", … in the review.
- "Statement N" is one review step per card whose Lean statement is new (or changed) in this run. Usually these are the target and the selected premises that Claude formalised, plus, in the round after you adopt a suggestion, that adopted card. The step shows your sentence above Claude's Lean, the "Fully explicit" toggle, "It uses" and "Show on the board". It is part of the proposal's files: Accept writes it. It has no accept or decline button of its own. It is a reading check, and if the Lean is wrong your only recourse is Feedback (a new round in which statements may change) or Discard.
- "Claude suggests" is a premise Claude thinks is missing: a new belief you might hold. It is usually offered when the target did not follow from your premises. Claude proposes it after the statements were frozen, and telelean checks in a separate scratch file, never in the files, that your selected premises plus this suggestion prove the target. That check gives the chip "closes the gap (checked)". The chip "gives the goal on its own: it may simply restate it" appears when your premises weren't needed. Both its sentence and its Lean are Claude's words.
  - It is not in the proposal's files, and Accept never writes it.
  - It appears as a translucent card at the top of the Assumptions column in the Proposed view (not a real card: you cannot select it and no arrows attach to it), and under "Premises Claude suggests" in the review's Result step.
  - It has its own decision. "I hold this" (an optional reason, then "Adopt") has telelean write it into Claude's working copy as your Assumption, worded by Claude. telelean also adds it to the target's premises and freezes the statements again, and a new round starts in which Claude proves the target with it; the current proposal is withdrawn. "No" declines it: the card disappears, the proposal stays open, and Claude is not told.
  - After adoption, the next round shows the adopted card as "+ new" on the board and as one of the "Statement N" steps, in Claude's italic style.
- In short: a Statement step asks "is this formalisation of a card faithful?" about content Accept will write. A "Claude suggests" card asks "do you believe this extra premise?". Saying yes changes your premise set and starts another proof round.
uncertainties: Nothing was run: every behaviour above comes from reading the code and the existing tests (unit, e2e and the runner's real-Lean engine test). It has not been confirmed in a live VS Code session.

'changed statement' (StatementReview.change === 'changed') looks unreachable in a proposal that passed the gate, because G3 'existing-changed' freezes every pre-run declaration. I did not find a test confirming either way.

Cards the user adds to the real board while a run is going would presumably show as '− removed' in the Proposed view: the diff compares the current real graph with the shadow graph, and Accept's merge keeps them. This is inferred from core/src/proposal/diff.ts and manager.buildProposal, not verified.

'Open in editor' on a card in the Proposed view probably opens the user's real file at the location from the proposal's (shadow's) graph, which may point at the wrong lines. This is inferred from LeanCode.tsx:73 and not verified.

A ghost suggested in an earlier round remains 'suggested', with its 'closes the gap (checked)' chip, after a Feedback round that may have changed the statements: no round filter exists in suggestedGhosts or the runner. Adoption re-freezes and the gate re-checks the proof, so this looks like a possibly stale display rather than a soundness hole.

ResultStep's hidden branch ('The result is shown after the statements…') appears unreachable through normal navigation, because reaching any step after the statements reveals the result. I may have missed an edge case where step indices shift.

How often implicit arguments, universes and coercions actually show in the Fully explicit form depends on the vocabulary rules. My claim that it is 'mostly notation in practice' rests on user-guide 10.14 (built-in types in signatures are refused; numerals allowed) and the test fixtures, not on a survey of real models.

That rejecting a ghost is never communicated to Claude in later rounds is based on rejectGhost (manager.ts:1615-1628) sending no turn, and feedbackTurn containing only the user's text. I did not check whether the context bundle of a later round lists rejected ghosts.
